## CURRENT ARCHITECTURE

- One browser PWA for desktop and mobile, using the existing HTTPS JSON API and PostgreSQL.
- Separate, replaceable client boundaries: **LocalStore** for persistence and **SyncEngine** for transfer orchestration.
- LocalStore stores structured records in IndexedDB. Its attachment adapter prefers filesystem storage when available and authorized, otherwise uses IndexedDB blobs, behind one read/write/delete contract.
- SyncEngine uses stable client UUIDs for idempotency and last acknowledged versions for optimistic concurrency. Sync runs on app launch, pull to refresh, and online local edits.

## CURRENT CONSTRAINTS

- Retain drafts and photos until authenticated success is acknowledged for that specific item. Timeouts, lost responses, expired sessions, validation failures, and partial chunk success do not authorize cleanup.
- Persist acknowledged transfer progress for interruption recovery. Preserve record-before-attachment ordering while allowing independent queue items to continue safely.
- Retry transient failures with capped exponential backoff and jitter. Validation requires correction; conflicts require explicit review, preserving the local draft and showing the server version. No automatic narrative merge.
- Adapter writes return persisted references only after storage succeeds. On IndexedDB quota or transaction failure, retain the working form in memory and report that it is unsaved. The partial filesystem-write failure policy remains unsettled.
- Use plain UTF-8 text with required-field and maximum-length validation. Show readable, screen-reader-accessible sync states; announce meaningful transitions, not every retry.
- Keep existing API names and endpoints. Exclude dashboards, analytics, push notifications, periodic background sync, and rich text. Design backlog and unconfirmed pilot scheduling do not change engineering scope.

## SUPERSEDED DECISIONS

- Native desktop client and desktop-wrapper fallback.
- localStorage as the production draft store.
- Filesystem-only attachments.
- WebSocket synchronization, including an optional optimization.
- Renaming the existing API to match the PWA package.

After those pass, integrate attachment transfer into SyncEngine and verify interruption recovery, expired authentication, lost responses, safe retries, and item-specific cleanup. Keep this work separate from analytics and new endpoints.
